name: What is the difference between office tenant improvement and office renovation?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between office tenant improvement and office renovation in a leased commercial space?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between office tenant improvement and office renovation in a leased commercial space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Office tenant improvement and office renovation overlap, but they are not always the same thing. Tenant improvement usually refers to construction done to customize a leased space for a specific occupant, often at move-in or lease turnover. Renovation is broader and can mean refreshing, reconfiguring, or modernizing an office that is already in use. Both may include demolition, new partitions, flooring, lighting, paint, cabinetry, and systems upgrades. The distinction matters because lease terms, landlord approvals, and allowances are usually tied to tenant improvement, while renovation may be planned as an owner-occupied or ongoing operational upgrade. In Los Angeles-area projects, the contractor should clarify whether the work is a base-building improvement, a tenant fit-out, or an occupied remodel. That affects permits, schedule, insurance, after-hours work, and who pays for what. If the goal is to move into a new suite in North Hollywood or Pasadena, tenant improvement is the more precise term to use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tenant improvement usually means tailoring a leased office to a new tenant’s needs, while renovation often means updating an existing office for continued use. In practice, both can involve walls, lighting, flooring, and mechanical work. The key difference is whether the work is tied to a lease turnover or an occupied-space upgrade.
